cards.info: What defines a positive relationship between two variables?
cards.backInfo: A positive relationship occurs when the dependent variable increases as the independent variable increases.

cards.info: What defines a negative relationship between two variables?
cards.backInfo: A negative relationship occurs when the dependent variable decreases as the independent variable increases.

cards.info: When is a relationship classified as having no apparent relationship?
cards.backInfo: When the dependent variable shows no consistent upward or downward trend as the independent variable changes.

cards.info: What is the first step of the 3-Point Slope Check?
cards.backInfo: Compare the first and last data pairs to determine the overall direction of change.
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A flowchart showing the three steps to identify a data relationship: Compare First/Last, Check Middle Pairs, and Estimate Differences.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/4f42f036-71ea-4604-a967-029e83d0cde2-1786506555302-408.webp)

cards.info: Why check middle data pairs in the 3-Point Slope Check?
cards.backInfo: To ensure the trend is consistent and not caused by a single outlier.
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A flowchart showing the three steps to identify a data relationship: Compare First/Last, Check Middle Pairs, and Estimate Differences.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/4f42f036-71ea-4604-a967-029e83d0cde2-1786506555302-408.webp)

cards.info: When is a data trend considered statistically consistent?
cards.backInfo: When the first-to-last direction matches at least half of the adjacent differences between points.

cards.info: In a negative relationship, how do the two variables move?
cards.backInfo: The two variables move in opposite directions (one increases while the other decreases).

cards.info: Is a single smaller increment enough to classify a trend as 'leveling off'?
cards.backInfo: No; a single smaller increment should not be mistaken for a change if the overall trend is consistent.

cards.info: What visual cue indicates no apparent relationship in a table?
cards.backInfo: Identical values at the start and end of the table indicate no apparent relationship.

cards.info: Does a single outlier negate an overall data relationship?
cards.backInfo: No; an outlier does not change the classification if the majority of data remains consistent.

cards.info: If both variables move in the same direction, what relationship exists?
cards.backInfo: A positive relationship, where the dependent variable increases as the independent variable increases.

cards.info: As $x$ increases, $y$ decreases. Identify this relationship type.
cards.backInfo: This is a negative relationship because the variables move in opposite directions.

cards.info: How does a 'scattered' data plot typically classify in ACT Science?
cards.backInfo: It is classified as having no apparent relationship because there is no predictable change.

cards.info: Which data pairs determine the overall direction in the 3-Point Slope Check?
cards.backInfo: The first and last data pairs are compared to determine the overall direction.
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A flowchart showing the three steps to identify a data relationship: Compare First/Last, Check Middle Pairs, and Estimate Differences.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/4f42f036-71ea-4604-a967-029e83d0cde2-1786506555302-408.webp)

cards.info: What is the second step when applying the 3-Point Slope Check?
cards.backInfo: Check one or two middle pairs to ensure the direction is consistent.
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A flowchart showing the three steps to identify a data relationship: Compare First/Last, Check Middle Pairs, and Estimate Differences.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/4f42f036-71ea-4604-a967-029e83d0cde2-1786506555302-408.webp)

cards.info: How many adjacent differences must match the overall direction for consistency?
cards.backInfo: The first-to-last direction must match at least half of the adjacent differences.

cards.info: Contrast variable movement in positive versus negative relationships.
cards.backInfo: Positive variables move in the same direction; negative variables move in opposite directions.

cards.info: Should you ignore minor fluctuations if the start-to-finish trend is clear?
cards.backInfo: Yes; do not mistake minor fluctuations or single small increments for a relationship change.

cards.info: What does a flat line on an ACT Science graph indicate?
cards.backInfo: A flat line indicates no apparent relationship between the variables.

cards.info: In what order should you read a table to determine trends?
cards.backInfo: Observe the dependent variable as the independent variable values increase numerically (left to right).
